+# ADR 0001: Raise Pricing Cache TTL to 3600 Seconds
+
+## Status
+
+Accepted
+
+## Context
+
+The pricing service currently caches responses with a time-to-live (TTL) of 900 seconds (15 minutes). This short cache window was implemented as a conservative measure to ensure pricing data remains relatively fresh, but it creates significant overhead under production load. Every 15 minutes, the cache expires across all clients, forcing simultaneous refresh requests to the pricing backend. This cache stampede pattern causes periodic spikes in backend load and increases operational latency during cache expiration windows. Additionally, pricing data typically changes infrequently in practice—most updates happen during maintenance windows or quarterly reviews—making the 15-minute window unnecessarily aggressive.
+
+Analysis of pricing update patterns shows that the vast majority of pricing changes are planned and announced in advance. Clients would benefit significantly from a longer cache duration that still respects the cadence of actual pricing changes. Extending the TTL to 3600 seconds (1 hour) aligns the cache lifetime with typical operational practices while reducing backend load and improving request latency for clients.
+
+## Decision
+
+We will increase the pricing cache TTL from 900 seconds to 3600 seconds. This change applies to all pricing service responses and will be coordinated with documentation updates to inform clients of the new cache behavior.
+
+## Consequences
+
+**Positive:**
+- Significantly reduced backend load due to fewer refresh requests and elimination of the 15-minute cache stampede pattern
+- Improved client-side latency as more requests will be served from cache
+- Reduced operational burden on the pricing service team during peak usage periods
+- Better alignment with actual pricing change frequency, reducing unnecessary cache invalidation
+
+**Negative:**
+- Pricing information may be stale for up to 1 hour after a change is published, which requires clear client communication about the cache behavior
+- If an emergency pricing adjustment is needed, clients will not see the update immediately; manual cache invalidation procedures must be documented and readily available for such scenarios
+- Existing clients relying on the 15-minute refresh window for real-time pricing data will need to implement alternative refresh strategies or accept the longer staleness window
+
+**Mitigations:**
+- Establish a documented process for emergency cache invalidation when immediate updates are required
+- Update API documentation to clearly specify the 3600-second cache TTL
+- Implement monitoring alerts for pricing update lag to track actual staleness in production
